hints: Focus on what Brønsted-Lowry theory is really about, proton donation and proton acceptance, not about salts or solvents.
Look at $\text{NH}_4^+$ turning into $\text{NH}_3$ and $\text{NH}_2^-$ turning into $\text{NH}_3$, one loses $\text{H}^+$, the other gains it.
Ask yourself which of the three statements actually describes proton transfer, and which just state other true facts that do not define an acid-base reaction.
walkthrough:
**Recall the Brønsted-Lowry definition**

Think simple and side by side. An acid is a proton ($\text{H}^+$) donor and a base is a proton ($\text{H}^+$) acceptor.

$$\text{acid} \rightarrow \text{conjugate base} + \text{H}^+$$

**Spot the proton transfer in this reaction**

Look at the nitrogen species. Ammonium loses a proton to become ammonia.

$$\text{NH}_4^+ \rightarrow \text{NH}_3 + \text{H}^+$$
And amide gains that proton to become ammonia.

$$\text{NH}_2^- + \text{H}^+ \rightarrow \text{NH}_3$$

**Test each statement**

Statement 1 is true and is exactly the Brønsted-Lowry idea, so it explains the classification. Statement 2 is true, $\text{Na}^+\text{Cl}^-$ is a salt, but salt formation does not prove proton transfer. Statement 3 is true, $\text{NH}_3$ has a lone pair and can act as a nucleophile, but that describes Lewis base behaviour, not Brønsted-Lowry proton transfer.

So only 1 explains why this is a Brønsted-Lowry acid-base reaction.

options.A: Incorrect. This would mean 1, 2 and 3 all explain the classification. While 1 is correct, 2 and 3 do not. Being a salt and being a nucleophile are true facts but they do not define Brønsted-Lowry proton donation and acceptance.
options.B: Incorrect. This would mean 1 and 2 together explain it. Statement 1 does, but statement 2 does not. Many reaction types produce a salt, for example precipitation, so saying $\text{Na}^+\text{Cl}^-$ is a salt gives no evidence of proton transfer.
options.C: Incorrect. This would mean 2 and 3 explain it but 1 does not. This is backwards. Statements 2 and 3 are true in general but irrelevant to Brønsted-Lowry theory, while statement 1 is the key proton donor idea that is missed here.
options.D: Correct. Only statement 1 explains the classification. $\text{NH}_4^+$ donates a proton to form $\text{NH}_3$, so it acts as a Brønsted-Lowry acid, and $\text{NH}_2^-$ accepts that proton, so it acts as a Brønsted-Lowry base.
